checks.note: Complete suite before adding the final fake-CLI integration test; production sources are unchanged.

checks.command: node --test --test-name-pattern="registered implementation worktree reaches Codex" test/workspace-access.test.ts

coverage: Original dirty checkout preserved; implementation starts at the recorded baseline.
Independent detached review snapshot stays pinned while implementation advances.
Durable creation intent is not replayed after an unknown Git outcome.
Cleanup requires terminal task, no active access, clean files including ignored content, and preserves branch history.
Repository policy, hooks, filters, index flags and path identity are checked before admission.
Duplicate writer access is rejected across SQLite connections; expiry and restart retain ownership until confirmed stop.
Permissions and requirement/code evidence are frozen; caller workspace paths are replaced with registered paths.
Cancellation during preparation prevents late process launch.
Snapshot tampering suppresses terminal evidence and marks the snapshot tainted.
Late events cannot reopen a failed stream; unknown process stop retains access.
Protected consultation runs through the controller without creating a branch.
Codex adapter receives the registered implementation worktree via a local fake CLI process.

ci.evidenceBinding: CI runs are keyed to the pushed commit. This local record does not assert a remote result.

limitations: No paid model calls or real target-project acceptance in M2.2.
HTTP and CLI service still expose only the simulation backend; M2.3 role handoff is not implemented.
Workspace locks are cooperative control-database ownership, not OS isolation. Native Codex sandbox permissions remain required.
Cross-service process reconciliation and automatic recovery of pending Git operations remain M3 work.
Git hooks/filters, fsmonitor, symlinks/submodules, hidden or sparse index entries require a separate trusted integration.
Real service enablement still requires auditing Codex MCP/hooks and controller-directory isolation.
